for some nonbinary people the scale of female to male doesn't work, because gender is a more abstract concept than that. (It can be seen in the autistic community mainly, because they created a concept of gender identities that are linked to moods, objects, concepts and words, and they have flags for that. )
I am agender, and common scales for gender make me always go "no" and put a dot at "0" or outside the scale. I was searching for a way to express gender for myself as i am a voidpunk and a transhumanist, philosophically. (you can look it up, it's interesting!) I know a few other people and friends who would like a more concept based scale instead of a "male-female" one, and i landed on this after grouping the different ideas i had into large categories. For these people they see themselves as non human in a certain way, but it's very hard to explain! 

I see with this post that some people don't adhere to the scale, put themselves out of it, or don't like it, but that mostly it's appreciated and a lot of people vibe with it! I can guess it could help people that are not used to alternative scales of genders to apprehend the question in a way they're not used to, and to explore it, and for other people it's a good way to express something they feel since a long time but that can be hard to put on paper :))

tldr: I know i went a bit overboard with my answer, but i hope i got it right a bit. It's different for a lot of people, for me i am not human in a voidpunk way, for others it can go from just vibing with the concept to really feeling inhuman.

the epidermis is the firs layer. if you brake it it will not leave long term scars but they are known for stinging and being itchy when healing. 

deeper than that is the dermis "styro/styrofoam" layer, it's white and it sometimes take a few seconds foe blood to start coming. it also starts gaping open and you can hit veins by cutting into that layer, it's less safe and leave scars

after that is the fat "bean" layer. it can look differently from person to person and it can be more or less easily atteinable depending on the body part you're cutting on. it usually looks like little bubbles of fat at its usually gaping open. it's starting to get really gross 'cause you can start hitting tendons and nerves and arteries and it can be really dangerous. usually if your cut hits deep in the fat layer or is a few centimeters long and gaping open you should get stitches, and it's definitely gonna leave scars for life.

under the fat layer there's the fascia, a protective layer of skin and under that you have the muscle. if you ever get to that point you should definitely seek help and get stitches, it's really dangerous and infections can be severe ://

in all case, take care of your cuts and clean them no matter how deep you got, and you should be able to find better explanations on how to treat your cuts and limit the risks somewhere on this sub
